reasons: The add form does not check email or LinkedIn formats.
Delete has only one confirmation prompt and no undo.
The list refreshes only when a change event arrives. If that event name changes in other code, the list goes out of date.

terms.meaning: The part of the app that saves and reads data for one topic, here the contacts.
A message sent inside the browser to tell other parts of the page that something changed.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in the page tools, the link tool, the shared header and footer, and the contact functions from the contacts store.
sections.why: The page needs these to read, save, search and delete contacts.

sections.name: ROLE_LABELS
sections.title: Short role labels
sections.what: Maps each contact role to a short tag shown on its card: HM, REFERRAL, CEO, EXEC, RECRUITER and OTHER.
sections.why: Short tags fit on a card.
sections.watch_out: Each role in the store needs an entry here. The TypeScript checker should flag a missing one.

sections.name: ROLE_COLORS
sections.title: Role tag colors
sections.what: Picks a color for each role tag: the accent color for hiring managers, blue for referrals, red for CEOs, purple for executives, and grey for recruiters and others.
sections.why: Color helps the user scan the list by role.
sections.watch_out: Two roles use fixed color codes while the others use theme colors, so those two stay the same in dark mode.

sections.name: ContactsPage (part 1)
sections.title: Page memory, loading and search
sections.what: Keeps the contacts list, the search text, whether the add form is open, and the new contact being typed. It loads contacts when the page opens and reloads them when the contacts-changed event arrives. Typing filters the list through the store's search function.
sections.why: Likely reason: the event listener keeps this page current when contacts are added from another page.
sections.watch_out: The page depends on other code sending the contacts-changed event. If that event name changes, the list will stop updating.

sections.name: ContactsPage (part 2)
sections.title: Add form, contact cards and delete
sections.what: When the add button is pressed, shows a form with name, company, title, role, LinkedIn, email, location and notes. Saving needs a name and a company. Below, each contact is a card with its name, title, company, location, role tag, links, notes, source and last contacted date. DELETE asks for confirmation first. An empty message appears when there are no contacts or no matches.
sections.why: Gives full manual control over the contacts list, with a confirmation step before deleting.
sections.watch_out: The confirmation prompt is the only protection against deleting a contact by mistake.

sections.name: ContactsPage (part 3)
sections.title: Closing the page layout
sections.what: Ends the main area and adds the shared footer and closes the page frame.

sections.name: inputStyle
sections.title: Form field style
sections.what: The look of the text boxes in the add form: padded, bordered, small monospace text.
sections.why: Keeps the form matching the rest of the app.

sections.name: smallBtn
sections.title: Small button and link style
sections.what: The look of the LinkedIn and email links on contact cards: small monospace text inside a thin bordered box.

summary: A contacts page where the user can search, add, view and delete the people they plan to reach out to.
purpose: Keeps one personal list of people at target companies, with their role and contact details, so they can be found later.
why: Gives the user one place to manage contacts, separate from the search panel on application pages. Reason beyond that is not stated in the code.
how: 1. The page loads all contacts when it opens and reloads them when a contacts-changed event arrives. 2. Typing in the search box filters the list by name, company, title, email or tag. 3. The add button opens a form, and saving requires a name and a company. 4. Each contact appears as a card with a role tag, links, notes and last contacted date. 5. DELETE removes a contact after a confirmation prompt.
inputs: Search text, new contact details from the add form, delete clicks, and the saved contacts from the contacts store.
outputs: A grid of contact cards, newly saved contacts, removed contacts, and messages for an empty list or no matches.
risks: Deleting asks for one confirmation and no undo is visible. The add form does not check email or LinkedIn formats. Search results depend on the search function in the contacts store, which is not shown here. Where the contacts are physically kept is decided by the store, not by this page.
debug: If a new contact does not appear, check the save function in the contacts store and whether the change event is sent. If search gives odd results, check the search function in the store. If a role tag shows the wrong label or color, check the role lists at the top of the file. If the save button stays disabled, both name and company must be filled in.
